title: Research Plans Are for Alignment
intro: Most research plans read like contracts written to survive scrutiny. A plan's real job is shared understanding.

learn.title: What a plan is for
learn.text:
Everyone should know **which decision the study informs**, **what success looks like**, and **their own role** — when to contribute, when to observe, when to step back.

Calabro's early-career plan had colour-coded transcripts and full sampling criteria. By slide 3, the PM was messaging someone else.

try.q: What is the real job of a research plan?
options: A record for the research repository
try.explain: Which decision, what success looks like, and everyone's role.

right.label: Written for alignment
items: How the team will use the results

learn.title: The one question
learn.text:
When a request arrives — “can you run a survey?” — the move is:

> “Yes, I can do that. But first, **what main questions are you hoping to answer with this research?**”

It shifts the conversation from method to goal, and it surfaces validation requests (“we've decided to build it and want proof people will like it”) without accusing anyone.

It also positions you as a collaborator rather than a critic.

try.q: Why does this question work better than challenging the method?
options: It takes less of the stakeholder's time
It avoids committing to a timeline
It gives you grounds to decline the work
try.explain: And it moves the conversation from method to goal. Not a critic.

learn.title: Then cascade
learn.text:
Follow-ups once the goal is on the table:

• Where are we in the build?
• Which decisions are still open?
• Do we need to track this over time?
• Are we comparing to something existing?

These questions decide the method far better than the original request did.

try.q: A stakeholder says they've already decided to build it and want proof people will like it. What has the question surfaced?
try.explain: Better to find that out before designing the study.

test.q: What went wrong with his early-career plan?
options: The PM stopped reading by slide 3
It was rejected by the research lead
It took too long to write
test.explain: Thoroughness isn't the same as alignment.

test.q: Which three things should a plan make clear?
test.explain: That is the alignment a plan exists to create.

test.q: What does the one question shift the conversation from?
test.explain: “What main questions are you hoping to answer?”

test.q: Which follow-up tells you whether you need a baseline?
options: Are we comparing to something existing?
Where are we in the build?
Do we need to track this over time?
test.explain: A comparison needs something to compare against.

test.q: Why do plans get over-written in the first place?
test.explain: Defensive thoroughness, aimed at the wrong audience.
